COMMENTS TO THE U.S. DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR ON THE DRAFT ENVIRONMENTAL IMPACT STATEMENT FOR PROPOSED IMPLEMENTATION OF EXECUTIVE ORDER 11644, PERTAINING TO USE OF OFF-ROAD VEHICLES ON PUBLIC LANDS.
JULY 7, 1972
My name is John W. Grandy, IV. I am Administrative Assistant for Wildlife at the National Parks and Conservation Association.

I appreciate the invitation of this Committee to submit the views of the NPCA on this important matter.
The National Parks and Conservation Association is the leading conservation organization concerned primarily with the protection of the National Park System, but also with other major environmental and conservation subjects such as wildlife and forestry.
We appreciate the opportunity to comment on the draft environmental impact statement pertaining to the use of off-road vehicles on public lands.
while the statement seems adequate in most places, alternatives to the proposed actions are insufficiently discussed.

The Secretary's memorandum (Page 3, paragraphs (a)(4) and (a)(5))
gives criteria for use of vehicles by area classifications such
as wilderness. The impact statement, however, considers all
areas as a group when considering alternatives.
27 Costs and benefits of the vehicle use pattern assigned, and alternative patterns, should be considered with reference to each area for which regulations (guidelines) are considered in (a)(4)
